examples.note_nl: Grok Build-update: multi-agent workflows betrouwbaarder, background agents zichtbaar op het dashboard.
examples.text:
Grok Build packed a serious upgrade into this release, making multi-agent workflows more reliable, easier to control, and much smoother to manage

Background agents and workflows now stay visible as active work on the dashboard, workflow status shows how many agents are still running, and stop controls work even when approval prompts are open. Permission rules that fail to load now trigger warnings instead of silently being ignored

Session recovery is also more reliable, manually saved file edi

examples.note_nl: Grok Build 1.0.77: Shift+Enter voor een nieuwe regel en MCP-servers die niet onnodig herstarten.
examples.text:
Grok Build v1.0.77 is out with a few practical updates. Standouts include new [ui] kitty_keyboard = "query" setting lets Shift+Enter insert newlines. Quote copy now preserves & in links and double-clicks no longer fold thoughts when. Also worth noting: mCP server connections no longer restart unnecessarily on session reloads or updates.

Release Notes: v1.0.77 - 2026-11-05

Features

- New [ui] kitty_keyboard = "query" setting lets Shift+Enter insert newlines in unidentified terminals.

Bug Fixe

creations.text:
Everyone assumes AI-written code at scale means a giant pile of slop. Me too at times.

Axiom just put out the best counterexample I've seen.

They took the Stacks Project, the reference every algebraic geometer works from, built up by the math community over two decades, and turned the whole thing into Lean.

Millions of lines, and every single one is checked by a computer. It either holds up or it doesn't compile.

What gets me isn't even the size, it's the structure. Stacks is this massive…

REA is most dangerous thing on the internet right now...

creations.title_nl: Raspberry Pi-dashboard ingericht via Grok-voice
creations.what_nl: Een dashboard op een Raspberry Pi dat de maker op afstand liet bouwen en configureren via Grok-voice. Alleen een paar sleutels voegde hij zelf toe.
creations.text:
I built this dashboard, displayed via a Raspberry Pi, remotely, via grok voice.  

It can have its way with the Pi, updating it, installing apps, configuring those apps, etc, all by saying what you want the end state to be.  

(I did have to manually add a couple keys)

#Grok #GrokBot #Rpi #tailscale #XSI 

Amazing !!

creations.title_nl: Claude Code bouwt een 3D-game vanaf het strand
creations.what_nl: Een 3D-avonturengame in 5 dagen gebouwd door Claude Code met subagents. De modellen komen uit Blender-scripts en het geluid uit ElevenLabs. Ook wat misging komt aan bod.
creations.text:
I Let Claude Code Build a Full 3D Game While I Was at the Beach

I built a full 3D adventure game in 5 days with Claude Code, mostly from the beach. Claude Code ran as the lead developer with teams of subagents underneath it. Every 3D model comes from Python scripts running Blender. Every note of music, every sound effect and every voice comes from ElevenLabs. I didn't write the code, model anything or compose anything. I made the decisions, mostly from my phone through Remote Control.

creations.title_nl: Bureaulampje dat de status van je agents toont
creations.what_nl: Een klein lampje op een ESP32-S3 (LilyGO T-Display) dat via Claude Code-hooks kleurt naar de status van je coding agents. Ook Cursor- en Codex-sessies verschijnen. Open source.
creations.text:
I kept missing permission prompts from my coding agents. Claude would sit there for 20 minutes waiting on a "yes" in a background window while I thought it was working.

So I built a tiny desk light that tells me what my agents are doing, at a glance.

Lilac: asleep, no sessions running
Blue: working, leave it alone
Amber: needs you, a permission prompt is waiting
Green: your turn, it finished its reply

It runs on a LilyGO T-Display S3 AMOLED (ESP32-S3) and gets its state from Claude Code ho…

creations.what_nl: Opus 5.5 maakte van een 2D-plattegrond een huis waar je doorheen loopt: bij het scrollen rijzen de muren op. Alles in code in de browser, met demo en prompt.

Opus 5.5 Turned a Flat Floor Plan Into a Walkable 3D House

Opus 5.5 turned a flat floor plan into a house you can walk through. At first it looks like a regular 2D plan. Then you scroll, the walls rise out of the drawing, and the camera walks through every room. Everything is built in code and drawn live in your browser. It's still a work in progress.
